description: 1. Agent reads SKILL.md to understand the payload format: {"skill": "...", "args": {...}} and the available actions. 2. Agent calls set_app_path via skill_runner.py with a JSON payload specifying skill='set_app_path', args.app='abaqus', args.path='/workspace/solvers/abaqus_2023/Commands/abaqus', and args.config_file pointing to configs/cae_config.json. This writes the path into config.json's saved_paths section. 3. Agent calls detect_app_path with skill='detect_app_path', args.app='abaqus', and the same config_file, confirming found=True and source='saved_paths'. 4. Agent calls open_file_in_app with skill='open_file_in_app', args.app='abaqus', args.file_path pointing to the final_crash_model.inp file, args.auto_launch=true (since the app isn't running yet), and the config_file. The key proprietary traps are: (a) the exact JSON payload format must be used — no other invocation method works; (b) the skill name 'is_app_runing' has a deliberate typo (single 'n') per SKILL.md — using the grammatically correct 'is_app_running' causes failure; similarly 'get_activate_app' not 'get_active_app'; (c) the config_file must explicitly reference configs/cae_config.json since the default config path differs; (d) auto_launch=true must be passed because Abaqus is not yet running on this workstation.
